You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC aligned panel analysis

Use when a divider separates same-size panels and output may be derived from aligned cell pairs.

## Exact evidence before abstraction
- Preserve each panel's exact cell values initially. For every demo, compare every aligned coordinate and record `(left value, right value) -> output value`.
- Group by exact ordered pair, then evaluate candidate predicates independently: exact equality, inequality, both-background, both-foreground, one-sided foreground, and pair-specific mappings.
- Do not collapse multi-valued/noisy panels into binary masks before evidence justifies it. A seemingly valid equality or intersection rule can be confounded if one pair category dominates observations.
- Record unchanged/exceptional pairs as carefully as output marks. One anomalous cell can invalidate a simple relation.

## Demo value and recovery
Before requesting a demo, name the unresolved pair category and explain which competing mappings it distinguishes in the test. After incorrect feedback, reset the whole relation and re-audit every coordinate across every demo; do not alter a few test cells or re-label the same unsupported rule as a mask operation. Request another pair when the ambiguity changes the predicted grid and the information is worth its cost.
